drivingQuestion: Under what conditions was Rabban Gamliel's rule for three women said?
outcomeNote: Rabban Gamliel answers that only the general principle applies

segments.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר לֹא כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים וְכוּ׳. תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: דַּנְתִּי לִפְנֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, יְלַמְּדֵינוּ רַבֵּינוּ בְּנָשִׁים זְרִיזוֹת אוֹ בְּנָשִׁים שֶׁאֵין זְרִיזוֹת? בְּעֵצִים לַחִים אוֹ בְּעֵצִים יְבֵשִׁים? בְּתַנּוּר חַם אוֹ בְּתַנּוּר צוֹנֵן? אָמַר לִי: אֵין לְךָ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁשָּׁנוּ חֲכָמִים, זֶה הַכְּלָל: תָּפַח — תִּלְטוֹשׁ בְּצוֹנֵן.
segments.en: It was taught in the mishna that «Rabbi Akiva says» that «not all women,» not all wood, and not all ovens are the same. «It was taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Akiva said: I deliberated» this matter «before Rabban Gamliel,» asking: «May our master teach us» if your statement, cited in the mishna, was said «with regard to diligent women or women who are not diligent?» Was it said «with regard to» an oven fueled with «moist wood or dry wood?» Was it said «with regard to a hot oven or a cold oven?» Rabban Gamliel himself «said to me: You have only what the Sages taught,» which is that «this is the principle:» If the dough begins to «rise» such that there is a concern that it may become leavened, «she should spread cold» water «onto» the dough to prevent it from becoming leavened.
